page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware environment includes 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a dedicated 944 GB local NVMe SSD. It features no GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions (avx512f, avx512_vnni, avx512_bf16) as well as hardware cryptographic accelerations such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by top 25% ratings in both stress-ng single-core (3080.08) and Geekbench single-core (1970.0), alongside strong text processing execution. In contrast, multi-core throughput and overall PassMark metrics position the instance squarely in the middle 50% band, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 11455.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 26254.61. Memory subsystem tests show solid cached bandwidth (1216.46 GB/sec for small blocks), but uncached read bandwidth drops to 37.92 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%. LLM inference results show strong text generation for smaller 135M models, but degrade significantly down to poor performance on 70B parameter models.

Given its high memory-to-core allocation and fast local NVMe temporary storage, the E16ads_v6 offers strong resource density for caching platforms, in-memory processing, and relational databases. Tradeoffs center on uncached memory throughput limits and moderate multi-core scaling, making it best matched for relational databases, Redis caching layers, medium-scale data analytics, and general memory-bound enterprise services rather than massive distributed parallel compute.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 128.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) paired with 944 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, operating without a discrete GPU. In benchmark assessments, it displays strong single-threaded execution, ranking in the top tier for Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, while delivering balanced middle-tier outcomes across multi-core CPU, compression, and general PassMark evaluations. However, uncached read memory bandwidth remains comparatively constrained. The combination of dedicated compute allocations, high memory capacity, and integrated NVMe storage makes the E16ads_v6 well suited for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory data caching with Redis, enterprise database backends, and memory-heavy ETL processing.
